note: Rewritten from the redescription (Portuguese) in Rocha & Cancello 2007; the original description is Emerson in Snyder 1949: 112, and the original publication was not used here, so the entry is marked as following the redescription. The original uses commas as decimal points, changed here to decimal points. The alate is described here for the first time (the original states that the alates of C. brevipilosus and C. macrognathus are described for the first time, while that of C. parvignathus is shown in Emerson 1925, fig. 82).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head is rectangular; in profile the dorsal margin is straight from the posterior third to the level of the fontanelle, where it is raised, and from the fontanelle to the base of the clypeus it forms a steep slope. In profile the head is not very thick, being thinner than in the other species of the genus. The labrum is pentagonal with distinct angles. The antennae have eleven segments, segment 1 twice as long as segment 2, the remaining segments subequal, segment 3 sometimes split. The mandibles are slender, curved inwards only at the tip, slightly less than half the head capsule length, each with a tooth at the base. The head bears setae, denser in the fontanelle region and sparser posteriorly, with few, scattered short hairs. The labrum bears 5—8 setae, the apical pair the longest. The postmentum has few setae, mainly anteriorly. The pronotum has few short hairs, with setae mainly along the margins; the remaining thoracic nota have few short hairs and many setae on the posterior margin; the abdominal tergites and sternites bear short hairs and setae, with a few erect setae on the posterior margin. Measurements (45 individuals, 6 specimens): head capsule length 1.54—1.84 mm, maximum head width 0.74—0.82 mm, head height 0.64—0.76 mm, maximum length of the left mandible 0.64—0.70 mm, mandible base to tip 0.64—0.70 mm, minimum length of the postmentum 1.12—1.44 mm, length of the left hind tibia 0.48—0.62 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The antennae have twelve segments; segment 1 is the longest, segment 2 is half as long as segment 1, the remaining segments are subequal, segment 3 sometimes subdivided. The head is densely covered with short hairs and setae. The thoracic nota bear short hairs and setae, the setae mainly on the posterior margin; the abdominal tergites and sternites are densely covered with short hairs and setae directed backwards, with few erect setae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head is oval; the compound eyes are large; the ocelli are oval, their distance from the compound eye equal to their minimum diameter; the fontanelle is oval, small and not projecting, at the level of the line joining the posterior margins of the compound eyes. The antennae have twelve or thirteen segments; segment 1 is the longest, segment 2 is half as long as segment 1, the remaining segments are subequal, segment 3 sometimes split. The head is covered with a continuous pile of short hairs and bears many erect setae. The pronotum is covered with a continuous pile of short hairs and with several scattered setae; the remaining thoracic nota are covered with short hairs; the abdominal tergites and sternites are covered with a continuous pile of short hairs, with setae mainly on the posterior margin, and the last 4 tergites and the posterior margin of all the sternites bear a few erect setae. The forewing is covered with short hairs, and the wing scale bears short hairs and many setae. In dorsal view the head has two pale spots above the ocelli. Measurements (6 individuals, both sexes, 2 specimens): head length 0.58—0.64 mm, maximum head width (including compound eyes) 0.80—0.88 mm, maximum diameter of the compound eye 0.24—0.26 mm, interocular distance 0.60—0.64 mm, maximum diameter of the ocellus 0.10 mm and minimum diameter 0.06—0.08 mm, maximum length of the pronotum 0.42—0.44 mm and maximum width 0.58—0.66 mm, length of the left hind tibia 0.68—0.78 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier has slender mandibles, which distinguishes it from Cylindrotermes brevipilosus and C. caata; the raised fontanelle region distinguishes it from Cylindrotermes macrognathus, C. flangiatus and C. capixaba; compared with C. sapiranga it is smaller, with a relatively narrower and thinner head, many setae and few short hairs.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The holotype is a soldier, deposited in the American Museum of Natural History, from Kartabo, Guyana, 1919-4-26, collected by A. E. Emerson. The species was described by Emerson in Snyder (1949: 112); Emerson (1925: 428) had earlier misidentified its alate and soldier under the name Cylindrotermes nordenskioeldi. Type locality: Kartabo, Cuyuni-Mazaruni, Guyana (6.38°N, 58.7°W).
